KEY MESSAGE 1...

993 mb surface low is now located over the western end of Lake
America. Aloft, a large closed off upper level low is located
over western NY and western PA. Our area remains within the
moist cyclonic flow around this storm system. Although the
storm's occluded front has passed through the area, widespread
clouds remain in place and upstream satellite imagery suggests
it will remain overcast through the rest of the day and into
tonight, as the large storm system is expected to only slowly
drift northeast towards northern New England for tonight, before
passing through Atlantic Canada for Saturday.

Regional radar imagery continue to show bands of light rain
showers rotating around the storm system. Our area has been
seeing occasional light showers, along with patches of drizzle
and mist, through the day so far. Based on the latest model 
guidance, there will be a more widespread area of showers and
light rain passing through the area this evening, as the storm
system slides by to the north. Despite the upper level passing
overhead, the boundary layer will be warm enough for nearly all
of this precip to be rain, and the light intensity of the
rainfall will prevent much dynamic cooling from occurring. The
highest peaks of the central Adirondacks could see some wet
snowflakes, but no accumulation is expected, with surface temps
holding steady across the region overnight in the mid 30s to low
40s.

As the storm departs, most areas will be fairly dry through much
of the day on Saturday. However, it will remain fairly cloudy
with plenty of lingering moisture around. With another upper
level disturbance passing by to the south for late in the day,
another round of evening showers are possible, although 
coverage won't be as widespread as Friday. P-type looks rain for
most areas, with any snow limited to the highest terrain with no
accumulation. Total rainfall amounts will be fairly light as
well, mainly under a tenth of an inch, so no impacts are
anticipated.

Some brief ridging is finally expected by Sunday. With some
drier air moving into the area, breaks in the cloud cover is
finally expected by later Sunday morning. Temps will be a little
milder than recent days thanks to the return of some sunshine,
with highs reaching into the low 50s for valley areas. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...

Another storm system is expected to impact the region for Sunday
night into Monday. This will be a fast moving storm system
riding in the west-southwest flow aloft. With the milder flow in
place, temps (both aloft and at the surface) will be warm enough
for precip to be rain for most areas, with just some high
terrain areas possibly seeing a changeover to snow on the
backside before ending, but even this is uncertain and would be
limited to only the highest peaks of the southern Adirondacks
and southern Greens.  Based on the latest NBM, total rainfall 
looks to range in the quarter to half inch range, although some 
locally higher totals are possible in the upslope favored areas 
of the western Adirondacks. With the limited rainfall amounts, 
no hydro issues are anticipated at this time. Main timing for
precip looks to be after midnight Sunday night and before noon
on Monday.

As the storm departs, it is expected to deepen as it passes
towards Atlantic Canada. With a strengthening surface gradient,
gusty west to northwest winds are expected behind the system for
Monday, especially in the afternoon hours, as some breaks in the
clouds occur and cooling temps aloft allow for better mixing.
Frequent winds gusts look to be in the 25 to 40 mph range across
much of the region. Latest NBM shows fairly high confidence 
(50% to 80% chance) for gusts to even exceed 40 mph in the
Mohawk Valley, Capital Region, eastern Catskills and Berkshires,
so there could be the possibility of some downed tree limbs and
power outages. Probabilities lower for gusts to reach or exceed
47 mph, but there is some localized areas where the probability
does reach 30%-50%, specifically in the Capital Region and
Berkshires, so some localized gusts in the solid Wind Advisory
criteria are possible. Will continue to monitor the wind
potential for Monday closely, as some wind impacts look to be a
possibility.
